Title and Commencement
1.This Act may be cited as the, " Copyright and Neighbouring
Rights Protection and Literal and Artistic Works Act, 2013", and shall
come into force, as from the date of signature .
Repeal and saving
2.(1) The following two Acts shall be repealed :-
(a) The Copy Right and Neighbouring Rights (Protection) Act
1996.
(b) the Literal and Artistic works 2001;
(2) Notwithstanding the Provisions of subsection (1) all regulations
and rules made thereunder shall remain in force until amended or
repealed In accordance with the provisions of this Act .

Scope of Application of the provisions of this Act

Protection of works
Works covered by protection
5. (1) The protection prescribed under the provisions of this Act
shall apply, without restriction by any formalities, to any
crealive work in the field of fiterature, science and arts, no
matter the way of expression thereln, or whatever its value,

8

(a) written works, such as book, magazine, periodical

(b) oral work like lectures and serom ;

(d) plays and musical plays or any other drama work ;
(e) work performed by movements, steps, or the
pantomime show ;
(f) the audio-visual work such as cinema, or audio­

(g) works of fine arts, whether they are sculpture,
drawlng, painting, decoration or works of applied arts

(i) works of architecture ;
(j) computer rrogramme ;
(k) maps of all kinds, portraits, sketches ancl relief map

(2) without affecting the protection of the original works, the

(a) translation, adaptation, summaries, modification,

(b) groups of protected or unprotected work, on

Works not included by protection
6. The protection prescribed under the provisions of this Act shall

Parti
Copyrights
Moral rights
7. (1) The author of the work shall have the following moral
rights to :-
(a) attribute the work to himself in his real or pseudonym
name, and he has the right to claim not to attribute
the work ln his name ;
(b) object to any distortion or mutation or alteratlon to
his work;
(c} object to any use of the work that may prejudice his
honour or reputatlon;
(d) disclose the work to the public for the first time and
specify the way and conditions of this disclosure
(e} withdraw the work from circulation for good reasons
on condition that he pays the aggrieved party a fair
compensation specified judicially or consentually
(2) Subject to the provisions of section 16, the moral rights
mentioned in paragraph (1) shall not be subject to
assignment or abandonment .
10

Economie rights
8. (1) The author of the work shall enjoy the exclusive economic
rights in the following situations :-
(a) copying of the work ;
(b) translation of the work, adaptation, musical
distribution or making any other modification on the
work;
(c) distribuling copies of the work to the public by way
of sale or expose for saie or any other act which

(d) hlring computer programmes, and this right does not
appiy unless they are the main object of the hir ing ;
(e) public performance ;
(f} transferring the work to the public .
(2) The author of the work may authorize any person to
exercise the rights mentioned in paragraph (1) provided
that the authorization shali be written and authorized by a
competent legal body •
The right of follow-up
9. (1) Where upon transfer of ownership of an original work of

(2) The regulalions shall specify the provisions which organize

Duration of protection
1 o. (1) Subject to the provisions of section 7(2) the protection of

ever;
Il

(2) ln relation to joint work the period shall start to run from

Ownership of Copyright and transfer of rights
Ownership of copyright
11. (1) Subject to the provisions of section 12(6) the rights

in the first instance to the author
12

Joint and collective works
12. (1) Where severat persons participate in the creation of a work

(2) Where several persons participate in the creation of a joint

(5) Where any infringement occurs to the joint work, each one

13

(6) The economic rights of the collective works shall vest into
the natural or corporale person who takes the Initiative and
the
the financial responsibility for creation of the collective

Audio-visual works
13. (1) Every person participates in the creation of an audlo-vlsual

rights

The author may waive to any persan any of his economic

(3) The authority to dispose the ownership of the material copy

Permission for exploitation
15. (1) The author of the work may give permission to exploit and

(2) The non exclusive permission to the permitted persan, may

(3) The exclusive permission gives only the permitted person

(4) The permission shall not deemed to be exclusive unless

(5) The owner of the copyright upon giving permission

permitted person specifies the business he is permitted to

Publishing contract
16. (1) The publishing contract shall be :-
{a) written and specifies the form and manner of

15

(b) clarifying the publisher commitment to give the

(3) Upon the death of a co-author ln joint works without leaving

Termination of contract by the author
17. With regards to the terms of the contract, the author may, where

in
(a) where lt is provided the contract for a specific period for

Transfer of ownership of copyright
after the author death
18. (1) On the death of the author his rights shall vest into his

(2) On the death of the author where he left no heirs, his rights

19.(1) Notwithstandlng the transfer of any of the economic rights of the

22. (1) Where on exptoiting a sound recording published for
way
commercial purpose by of broadcasting, transfer to the

Chapter IV

any
